name: Predictive Maintenance
blurb: Using AI to anticipate equipment and instrument failures.
title: Predictive Maintenance
answer: Predictive maintenance uses sensor and usage data to forecast failures before they stop a line or invalidate a test. It is a low regulatory risk starting point because the AI advises maintenance teams rather than deciding product quality, and automation programmes that include maintenance alerts report strong returns.

reading.body:
Predictive maintenance is the low-risk entry point for AI in life sciences manufacturing because it advises maintenance teams rather than deciding product quality.

The pattern is a deliberate ordering of ambition. Sensor and usage data forecast equipment and instrument failures before they stop a line or invalidate a test, and the AI's output goes to people who can act on it. Because the model does not touch product quality decisions, it sits outside the heaviest regulatory scrutiny that governs quality critical uses. Roche Diagnostics reported returns from laboratory automation that included reduced manual work and errors, which is the kind of operational gain that funds the next step.

For AI specifically, the value is in the sequence. A team that builds data pipelines and trust on maintenance alerts has the sensor coverage, the data integrity habits, and the internal credibility needed before attempting quality critical applications. Skipping that step means asking a regulator and a validation team to trust a model before the organisation has learned to trust its own data.

What this does not tell the reader is how much any of it costs, how long it takes, or whether the returns hold outside the one reported case. The evidence here is a single automation programme, not a survey of maintenance deployments.

explainer:
Unplanned equipment failures stop production lines and can invalidate laboratory tests, both costly in a regulated plant where restarting requires checks and documentation. Predictive maintenance uses data such as vibration, temperature, power draw, run hours and error logs to forecast when equipment is likely to fail, so it can be serviced beforehand.

Because maintenance predictions advise people rather than decide product quality, they carry less regulatory burden than quality critical uses, which makes them a good first AI project in a plant. They also force the groundwork, connecting equipment, collecting clean data and building pipelines, that later quality uses need.
